ca_pyramid_tower_and_the_stirrup.blurb: Pyramid Tower and The Stirrup are neighbouring formations in the Stirrup Towers group at Stirrup Tank, in the Pinto Basin of Joshua Tree National Park. There are eight routes: six trad leads and two top-rope lines, running from 5.4 to 5.10. Half of them sit at 5.10, and a few moderates between 5.4 and 5.6 give newer leaders something to climb. The formations offer a mix of crack and face climbing on monzogranite, with some routes carrying bolts. Both are only a few minutes on foot from the parking loop.

ca_salmon_lake_south.blurb: Salmon Lake South is a small, low wall near Salmon Lake in the Rainbow area off the I-80 corridor, west of Donner Pass. It has eight lines: four top-ropes, three trad leads and a single boulder problem, mostly cracks and juniper-assisted lines between 5.6 and 5.10. The cliff is short, so it suits a side trip for hikers or backpackers who already have a light rack along. Reaching it takes a hike to the lake and a few minutes further south on foot, with views over the surrounding country from the base.

ca_slump_rock.blurb: Slump Rock is a squat, round formation among the Roadside Rocks west of Park Boulevard, between the Hidden Valley and Lost Horse parts of Joshua Tree National Park. All eight routes are trad leads. Grades start at 5.6, with three at 5.7 and three at 5.10, plus one harder 5.11 line, so there is a spread from beginner leads to steady 5.10 cracks. A few of the routes carry an R rating, and the climbs are short. The base is a brief stroll across open desert from the road.
ca_slump_rock.approach: A short walk across open desert from the road to the base of the rock.

ca_juggernaut_the.blurb: The Juggernaut is a peak on the north side of Sawtooth Ridge in the High Sierra, within the Hoover Wilderness and just beside the much larger Incredible Hulk. It has eight alpine routes, typically around five pitches, with five at 5.10 and three at 5.11. Climbs are trad and run up cracks, corners and arches. Getting there is a long backpack from Twin Lakes by way of Robinson Creek, Barney Lake and Mule Pass, followed by a rocky gully and cairns to the base; plan roughly three to three and a half hours. Camping near the base is good.
